meta.tagline: The capital of Puglia — and the street where grandmothers sit in their doorways making orecchiette (Puglia's handmade pasta) by hand

pills: Buy focaccia barese fresh from the bakery in the morning

overview.intro: Bari sits on the Adriatic coast in southern Italy, the capital of the Puglia region. It's different from northern Italy's polished cities — life here is lived on the street. In the labyrinthine alleys of Bari Vecchia, grandmothers roll orecchiette in their doorways, focaccia aromas drift from bakeries in the morning, and fishermen sell the morning catch at the harbour. The city is raw and alive, and that energy draws you in. Tourist pressure hasn't reached Venice or Rome levels yet — which means it still offers a genuinely local experience. It's also the perfect base for exploring Puglia: Alberobello, Matera and the Adriatic coves are all day-trip distance.

local_word.definition: Puglia's handmade pasta — the name means 'little ears' in Italian. Shaped by pressing with the thumb, producing small pasta pieces thin in the middle and thicker at the edges. The classic version served with cime di rapa (turnip tops), garlic, chilli and sometimes anchovies is the most representative dish of Puglia. Watching the local women on Strada delle Orecchiette make this pasta by hand — and buying it fresh — is both a meal and an experience.

rules.title: Enter Bari Vecchia in the early morning hours
rules.description: Bari's historic old neighbourhood is completely different in the morning. Street vendors are setting up their stalls, bakeries are opening, grandmothers are beginning to roll orecchiette. Tourists and crowds grow in the afternoon. Between 8am and 10am is both the quietest and most authentic moment. For focaccia barese, getting it fresh from the bakery at this hour is essential.

rules.title: Don't skip Strada delle Orecchiette
rules.description: A narrow street inside Bari Vecchia, also known as Arco Basso. Local women have been rolling handmade orecchiette here in their doorways for centuries and selling it. Taking fresh orecchiette home or simply watching on the spot — this street is one of Bari's most authentic experiences. Most lively between 9am and 12pm. €3-5 per packet.

rules.title: Use it as a base for exploring Puglia
rules.description: From Bari: Alberobello 1 hour (by FSE bus), Matera 1.5 hours, Polignano a Mare 30-45 minutes, Lecce 1.5 hours. All these destinations are reachable by train or bus and ideal for day trip planning. Staying in Bari and exploring the surroundings is both practical and economical.

quick_facts.label: Airport
quick_facts.sub: Ferrotramviaria train to centre ~20 min · ticket ~€5 · taxi ~€25

quick_facts.label: Transport
quick_facts.sub: AMTAB ticket €1-1.20 (75 min) · train ideal for all of Puglia

quick_facts.label: Weather
quick_facts.sub: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct ideal · Jul–Aug hot · Dec–Feb mild and rainy

tip.label: Lungomare — ideal for the evening passeggiata
tip.text: Bari's seafront promenade Lungomare Nazario Sauro fills with Barilesi (Bari locals) taking their evening stroll between 6pm and 8pm. The passeggiata is an inseparable part of Italian culture. Free, authentic, with Adriatic views. Most beautiful at sunset.

overview.title: Welcome to Bari

transport.intro: Bari's historic centre is walkable. AMTAB buses cover the city; regional trains are ideal for all of Puglia.

items.title: Airport → Bari centre
items.description: Ferrotramviaria train from the airport to Bari Centrale in approximately 20 minutes, ticket around €5. Departures every 30-60 minutes. AMTAB bus also provides a connection but can take longer due to traffic. Fixed-price taxi approximately €25. The train is definitely the most practical option.

items.title: AMTAB — city buses
items.description: Bari's city bus network. Single fare €1-1.20, valid for 75 minutes. Tickets from tabacchi (tobacconists) or edicole (newsstands). When you board, don't forget to validate your ticket in the machine. Buses are used for the Lungomare and Pane e Pomodoro beach. The historic centre is within walking distance.

items.title: Regional train — for exploring Puglia
items.description: From Bari Centrale, connections to all of Puglia. Alberobello: ~1 hour by FSE bus (€5-8) or 1.5-2 hours by connecting train. Polignano a Mare: 30-45 minutes, €3-5. Lecce: 1.5 hours (regional train €10-15, fast train €15-35).

items.title: Car hire — for coastal exploration
items.description: Using a car within Bari city is actually unnecessary — traffic is heavy and parking is difficult. However, a car offers freedom for exploring the Puglia coast and reaching spots that trains don't serve. Plan the hire from outside Bari centre.

items.title: Walking — ideal for the historic centre
items.description: Bari Vecchia, Piazza Mercantile, Basilica di San Nicola, Castello Svevo, Lungomare and the Murat neighbourhood are all walkable — compact and close together. Comfortable shoes essential for Bari Vecchia's narrow streets. Best hours for walking on sunny days are morning and evening.

callout.label: Polignano a Mare — 30 minutes from Bari
callout.text: A small town built on a rocky promontory jutting into the Adriatic. 30 minutes from Bari by train, €3-4. Cave beaches carved into the rock, crystal Adriatic water, narrow white streets. Birthplace of Domenico Modugno (composer of Volare). Very crowded in the afternoon in midsummer — go early in the morning or choose September-October. Free entry.

transport.title: Getting Around

stay.intro: In Bari, Bari Vecchia or the Murat neighbourhood are the best locations — both are central but their characters are very different.

local_word.definition: Bari's modern neighbourhood planned in the 19th century by French governor Joachim Murat — wide boulevards, orderly grid plan, Neo-classical buildings. The complete opposite of Bari Vecchia's chaotic labyrinth. Via Sparano shopping street, cafés, restaurants and boutiques are all here.

items.name: Bari Vecchia — the historic old town
items.description: Narrow stone streets, Baroque churches, focaccia aromas. Basilica di San Nicola and Castello Svevo within walking distance. Quiet and impressive in the morning hours. Some streets are still rough and unrestored but that's part of the authenticity.

items.name: Murat — modern centre
items.description: Wide boulevards, close to Bari Centrale. Via Sparano shopping street. 10 minutes walk to Bari Vecchia. Comfortable hotels with good connections.

items.name: Around the Lungomare
items.description: On the Adriatic coast. Close to the free Pane e Pomodoro beach. On the evening passeggiata route. 15-20 minutes walk to Bari Vecchia.

items.name: Japigia — local neighbourhood
items.description: To the south, a little further from the historic centre. No tourists but local trattorias and neighbourhood life. Budget-friendly. 15 minutes to the centre by bus.

items.name: Polignano a Mare
items.description: 30 minutes from Bari, a small town on an Adriatic cliff. Completely different when the midday crowds leave. Small hotels and B&Bs available.

stay.title: Where to Stay

best_time.intro: Bari can be visited year-round — summer is hot but lively, spring and autumn are the most balanced.

items.label: Spring
items.name: The best time
items.description: April and May are Bari's golden period. Temperatures 18-24°C, no crowds, orecchiette season at its best with fresh vegetables. Puglia's olive groves and flowering countryside are unmissable views during this period. Ideal through to mid-June.

callout.label: April in Puglia — blossoming olive groves
callout.text: In April, almond and cherry trees blossom in Puglia's interior. Roads through Valle d'Itria and the Trulli region are covered in pink blossom. One hour by car from Bari. Timing is perfect for both Bari and Puglia exploration during this period — space in hotels and restaurants everywhere.

items.subtitle: Spring · Mild weather, fewer crowds, Puglia at its finest

items.label: Summer
items.name: Hot and lively
items.description: July and August are hot but Bari Vecchia's narrow streets are shaded. The Lungomare fills with life in the evenings. Pane e Pomodoro beach is still breathable on weekday mornings. Polignano a Mare gets very crowded in the afternoon — go early. Southern Italy's summer evening culture is at its most vibrant during this period.

callout.label: Pane e Pomodoro — Bari's free beach
callout.text: South of the Lungomare, a free city beach reachable on foot or by bus. Free beaches on Italy's coast are rare — which makes this very valuable. Fine sand, clean water. Weekday mornings between 8am and 10am have few crowds. Weekend afternoons get very full. Bring your own umbrella or towel.

items.subtitle: Summer · 30-35°C, swimming in the Adriatic, long evenings

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Second best time
items.description: September and October are excellent for Bari. Temperatures 22-26°C, the Adriatic is still swimmable. Puglia's olive harvest in October-November. The orecchiette con cime di rapa season begins — turnip tops are at their finest in autumn. November brings more rain but prices drop significantly.

callout.label: Olive harvest — October-November in Puglia
callout.text: Puglia is one of the world's largest olive oil producers. October-November is the olive harvesting season. Some family estates invite visitors into the harvest process and offer freshly pressed olive oil tastings. Research estates around Bari in advance. Buying fresh olive oil (olio nuovo) is the best opportunity of the year during this period.

items.subtitle: Autumn · Summer crowds gone, sea still warm, harvest season

items.label: Winter
items.name: Quiet and affordable
items.description: From December to February Bari is mild and quiet by southern Italian standards — the city doesn't really get cold, averaging 10-15°C. Some rainy days but plenty of sunny moments too. Bari Vecchia in the morning hours is empty and impressive. Winter trattorias serve tiella barese and bombette at their finest. Prices noticeably lower.

callout.label: Bari in winter — Christmas markets and the focaccia ritual
callout.text: In December, Christmas markets set up in Piazza Mercantile. Winter mornings — buying focaccia barese from the bakery and eating it by the sea — are a local ritual. Basilica di San Nicola is nearly empty in winter.

items.subtitle: Winter · 10-15°C, empty museums, winter dishes

best_time.title: When to Go

monthly_highlights.text: Festa di San Nicola: the saint's statue goes out to sea, with processions and fireworks — the city's greatest feast.
Sea season: Pane e Pomodoro beach and the southern coves; at night the lungomare becomes an open-air living room.
The ideal season: the sea still warm, Puglia's harvest and sagre (local food festivals) back to back.
San Nicola's winter day: Santa Claus honoured in his own city; lights, liturgies and the first scent of panettone.

eat.intro: Food in Bari is both cheap and delicious — street food culture is strong, focaccia is the morning ritual, orecchiette is made by hand.

local_word.definition: Bari's focaccia is different from other Italian regions: boiled potato is folded into the dough, making it extraordinarily soft. Topped with cherry tomatoes, Barese olives, sea salt and plenty of olive oil. At its most delicious when fresh from the oven in the morning. €2-4. Barilesi eat focaccia hot, holding it in their hand — eating it while walking down the street is the true Barese way.

items.name: Focaccia barese
items.description: Bari's defining food. Panificio Fiore (Via Calefati) comes out fresh from the wood-fired oven at 8:30am — go early for this address. Alternative: small bakeries inside Bari Vecchia. Eat it hot — still delicious when cool but there's a difference. €2-4. Walking out of the shop and eating in the street is the true Barese way.
items.tag: Panificio Fiore · Bari Vecchia bakeries · fresh in the morning · €2–4

items.name: Panzerotto
items.description: Bari's own fried dough — tomato and mozzarella filling inside. Puffs up in the frying oil and turns golden. Crispy outside, hot and yielding inside. Venezia 40 (on the Lungomare, facing the Adriatic) is the most famous address. Can have a queue from 6pm onwards. €3-5.
items.tag: Venezia 40, Lungomare · €3–5 · crowded in the evening — go early

items.name: Orecchiette con cime di rapa
items.description: Puglia's most representative dish — handmade little-ear pasta, turnip tops, garlic and chilli. The essence of the dish is simple but ingredient quality changes everything. Turnip tops are at their finest in winter. €8-12 at local trattorias in Bari Vecchia and Murat.
items.tag: Local trattorias · €8–12 · ask for freshly made

items.name: Sgagliozze
items.description: Fried polenta slices made from cornmeal — the evening street food of Bari Vecchia. A stall sets up and sells them at Largo Albicocca at certain hours. Crispy outside, soft inside, with salt on top. €1-2. Simple but addictive. Perfect alongside a glass of Primitivo at aperitivo hour.
items.tag: Largo Albicocca, Bari Vecchia · €1–2 · midday and evening hours

items.name: Crudo di mare — raw seafood
items.description: Eating raw seafood at the Adriatic's edge is a Barese tradition. At the N'dranghet fish market near the old harbour, fresh mussels, sea urchins and octopus can be eaten straight from the morning catch. Fresh and cheap — it may take some courage. Also available at fish stalls within Bari Vecchia.
items.tag: N'dranghet fish market, old harbour · early morning · fresh and cheap

items.name: Pasticciotto and sporcamuss
items.description: Puglia's pastry culture: pasticciotto (a small shortcrust tart with custard filling, originally from Lecce but everywhere), sporcamuss (a flaky pastry with sugar and custard — the name means 'dirty your mouth'). Both ideal for breakfast or an afternoon café break. €1.50-3 at pastry shops.
items.tag: Bari pastry shops · €1.50–3 · morning or afternoon

callout.label: Aperitivo culture — with Primitivo wine
callout.text: Aperitivo hour in Bari (6pm-8pm) is the most enjoyable pause of the day. At bars and osterias, Puglia's Primitivo or Negroamaro red, Fiano white or an Aperol Spritz, alongside complimentary sgagliozze and taralli. Bars in the Murat neighbourhood and osterias near Bari Vecchia are the liveliest at this hour. A glass €4-7.

eat.title: What to Eat

hidden_gems.intro: Bari's finest corners are in the labyrinth of Bari Vecchia, along the coastline and just beyond short train journeys.

items.name: Strada delle Orecchiette (Arco Basso)
items.description: A narrow street inside Bari Vecchia, known as Arco Basso. Local women have been rolling orecchiette, cavatelli and other handmade pasta here in their doorways for centuries. Ask permission before taking photos, buy fresh pasta. Most lively between 9am and 12pm. €3-5 per packet — the finest Puglia souvenir.
items.rarity: The street where grandmothers roll pasta in their doorways

items.name: Basilica di San Nicola
items.description: An 11th-century Norman-Romanesque basilica in the heart of Bari Vecchia. It's believed that the relics of Saint Nicholas — who inspired Father Christmas — are kept here. Free entry. Downstairs to the crypt — dim light, columns and Saint Nicholas's sarcophagus. Go early for the morning service.
items.rarity: Rarely visited — but Bari's most beautiful building

items.name: Polignano a Mare
items.description: Cave beaches carved into Adriatic rock, crystal water, narrow white streets. 30 minutes from Bari by train. Very crowded in the afternoon — quiet between 8am and 10am. Lama Monachile cove is the finest photo spot. Free entry.
items.rarity: From cliff to Adriatic — 30 minutes by train

items.name: Alberobello — Trulli village
items.description: 1 hour 20 minutes from Bari by train. UNESCO World Heritage Site. White trulli houses with conical stone roofs — this architecture exists only here, in the Valle d'Itria. Rione Monti neighbourhood: hundreds of trulli side by side. Empty and impressive in the early morning hours. Easy day trip from Bari.
items.rarity: Found nowhere else in the world — conical stone houses

items.name: Matera
items.description: About 1.5-2 hours from Bari by train and bus. UNESCO World Heritage Site and 2019 European Capital of Culture. Sassi (cave houses) carved into the rock face — people have lived here for 9,000 years. Rocky panorama facing the Gravina valley, cave churches, restaurants in stone streets. A day trip is possible from Bari but staying overnight is better.

items.name: Castel del Monte
items.description: 1 hour from Bari by car, near Andria on a hilltop. An octagonal castle from the 13th century — built by Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II. Why octagonal? The courtyard is octagonal, eight towers are octagonal, eight rooms on each floor. The answer is still debated. On the UNESCO list, a symbol of Puglia. The interior is relatively plain but the architecture and views are impressive. Ticketed.

callout.label: Piazza Mercantile — espresso at the heart of the morning
callout.text: Bari Vecchia's main square. The city's trading and meeting point since the Middle Ages. Colonna della Giustizia (the Justice Column) stands in the centre. The cafés surrounding it fill with local businesspeople and shopkeepers between 7am and 9am. A €1 espresso, standing at the counter — this is Italy's most authentic morning ritual. Sit and watch: the square's energy captures Bari perfectly.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Gems

items.label: Eat focaccia barese — fresh from the morning bakery
items.sub: Panificio Fiore at 8:30am. €2-4. Eat it hot while walking the street. A Bari ritual.

items.label: Visit Strada delle Orecchiette
items.sub: Bari Vecchia, Arco Basso. 9am-12pm. Grandmothers' handmade pasta. Ask permission before photos.

items.label: Go to Basilica di San Nicola
items.sub: Bari Vecchia. Free entry. Go down to the crypt. 11th-century Norman-Romanesque architecture.

items.label: Try panzerotto — at Venezia 40
items.sub: Lungomare. €3-5. Crowded in the evening — go at 5pm. Tomato and mozzarella filling.

items.label: Walk the Lungomare in the evening passeggiata
items.sub: 6pm-8pm. Walk with Barilesi, Adriatic sunset. Free. Italian evening ritual.

items.label: Try sgagliozze — at Largo Albicocca
items.sub: Bari Vecchia. €1-2. Fried polenta slices. Perfect with Primitivo wine at aperitivo hour.

items.label: Go to Polignano a Mare
items.sub: Train from Bari, 30-45 min, ~€3-5. Go between 8am and 10am. Lama Monachile cove. Free.

items.label: Take a day trip to Alberobello
items.sub: FSE bus from Bari, ~1 hour, ~€5-8. Trulli houses. UNESCO. Less crowded in the early morning.

items.label: Try crudo di mare — at the old harbour
items.sub: N'dranghet fish market. Early morning. Raw mussels, sea urchins. Fresh.

items.label: Get lost in Bari Vecchia — early morning
items.sub: Between 8am and 10am. Narrow stone streets, bakery aromas, cats and shopkeepers.

items.label: Eat orecchiette con cime di rapa
items.sub: Local trattoria. €8-12. Ask for freshly made. Turnip tops are most delicious in winter.

items.label: Go to Matera
items.sub: Train + bus, ~1.5-2 hours. UNESCO. 9,000-year-old cave city. Day trip possible, overnight is better.

checklist.title: Bari Checklist
checklist.completion_message: Bari won you over on the first day — Puglia will draw you back again.

traps.title: Skip the Traps
traps.intro: Bari hasn't yet surrendered to tourism; its traps are few, but the day-trip circuit has things worth knowing. These four suffice.

items.name: Packaged 'handmade' orecchiette
items.description: The nonnas of Arco Basso truly roll pasta at their doorsteps; but some stalls sell factory pasta as 'handmade'.
items.instead: Buy from the stall where you watched it being made; fresh lasts two days refrigerated — ask for the dried kind to travel.

items.name: Crudo di mare courage at a random spot
items.description: Raw seafood is a Bari tradition, but never from a stall waiting in the heat; don't let your stomach end the holiday early.
items.instead: Eat crudo at established addresses: the fishermen's own stand by the harbour or known ristorantes — fresh, on ice, safe.

items.name: Arriving in Alberobello with the noon coach convoy
items.description: The trulli village becomes a tour-bus flood at midday; the fairytale set turns into a selfie queue.
items.instead: Take the first morning train or sleep there: at sunrise the trulli lanes are yours alone.

items.name: Driving to Polignano, driving into the old town
items.description: Parking in Polignano is near-impossible in summer; steering a car into Bari Vecchia's lanes is a mistake in itself.
items.instead: The train to Polignano takes 20 minutes; in Bari, walk the old town — it's no bigger than your palm anyway.

callout.label: The golden rule
callout.text: Bari lives with its doors open: the nonna's pasta table, the saint's basilica, the neighbours' street chat. Those who look for closed doors are tourists; those who walk through open ones become guests.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: Old town, orecchiette and the seafront

steps.title: Bari Vecchia morning
steps.description: Get lost in the lanes: washing lines, saints' corners, doorstep conversations. The city at its most honest.

steps.title: Basilica di San Nicola
steps.description: The Romanesque basilica holding Santa Claus's (Saint Nicholas's) bones; the crypt is where Catholic and Orthodox pilgrims meet.

steps.title: Strada delle Orecchiette
steps.description: Watch the nonnas roll pasta at their doors on Arco Basso; buy fresh orecchiette from the stall.

steps.title: Lunch — focaccia or raw sea
steps.description: Hot focaccia barese from Panificio Fiore, or crudo courage by the harbour; both are Bari classics.

steps.title: Lungomare walk
steps.description: Walk against the sea on one of Italy's longest waterfronts, as far as the Margherita Theatre.

steps.title: Dinner — orecchiette con cime di rapa
steps.description: The city's signature pasta at a trattoria + Primitivo wine; close with a pasticciotto.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the city as a guest, not a tourist

steps.title: The Bari classics
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: old town, basilica, orecchiette, lungomare.

steps.title: Polignano and the coast
steps.description: Morning train to Polignano a Mare: the Lama Monachile cove, cliff terraces, a special gelato. Monopoli's harbour in the afternoon, back to Bari at night.

steps.title: Trulli or the stone city
steps.description: Choose: Alberobello's trulli lanes at first light, or Matera's sassi cave houses (easy by train). A farewell panzerotto on return.

phrases.title: The 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Italian is enough, but a pinch of Barese makes you a man of the street.

items.meaning: Hi / bye — any hour, to anyone
Please — add it to the end of your order
Cheers! — Primitivo glasses rise to this
The Barese greeting: 'hey there, beautiful!' — hear it and you belong to the neighbourhood
